{{Conservatism in Iran|Intellectuals}}
'''Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel''' ({{langx|fa|غلامعلی حداد عادل}}; born 9 May 1945)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://haddadadel.ir/biography/88-890724.html |title=اطلاعات شخصی |website=haddadadel.ir |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150121035646/http://haddadadel.ir/biography/88-890724.html |archive-date=21 January 2015}}</ref> is an Iranian politician and former chairman of the [[Parliament of Iran|Parliament]]. Haddad-Adel is a member of the [[Expediency Discernment Council]].

He was the first non-cleric in the post since the [[Iranian Revolution]] of 1979. He was one of the candidates in the [[2013 Iranian presidential election|2013 presidential election]] but withdrew on 10 June, four days before the election.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.timesofisrael.com/hardline-candidate-withdraws-from-iran-election/ |title= Hardline candidate withdraws from Iran election |publisher= The Times of Israel}}</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130618034236/http://www.iranelect.ir/showpage.aspx?id=78116&title=%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%B5%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%81-%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF|title=حداد عادل از ادامۀ رقابت‌ها انصراف داد + بیانیۀ وی}} Iran Elect</ref> He is part of "neo-[[Iranian principlists|principilist]]" group in the Iranian political scene.<ref name=farzan13>{{cite web|last=Sabet|first=Farzan|title=The Islamic Republic's political elite and Syria|url=http://iranmediaresearch.org/en/system/files/islamicrepublics_politicaleliteandsyria.pdf?download=1|work=IranPolitik|access-date=30 July 2013|format=Special Report|date=June 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130711044804/http://iranmediaresearch.org/en/system/files/islamicrepublics_politicaleliteandsyria.pdf?download=1|archive-date=11 July 2013}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Haddad-Adel was born in Tehran on 9 May 1945 into a business family.<ref name=usip>{{cite web|title=Iran's Political Elite|url=http://iranprimer.usip.org/resource/irans-political-elite|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101028103141/http://iranprimer.usip.org/resource/irans-political-elite|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 October 2010|work=United States Institute of Peace|date=11 October 2010 |access-date=28 July 2013}}</ref><ref name=ireview>{{cite web|title=Biographies of Eight Qualified Candidates for Iran Presidential Election|url=http://www.iranreview.org/content/Documents/Biographies-of-Eight-Qualified-Candidates-for-Iran-Presidential-Election.htm|work=Iran Review|access-date=13 August 2013|date=22 May 2013}}</ref> He received a bachelor's degree in physics<ref name=yonah/> from the University of Tehran and also, a master's degree in physics from [[University of Shiraz]]. He also holds a PhD in philosophy<ref name=yonah/> from the [[University of Tehran]] which he received in 1975.

He studied [[Islamic philosophy]] under [[Morteza Motahhari]] and also under [[Seyyed Hossein Nasr|Sayyed Hossein Nasr]], a noted critic of [[Marxism]].{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

==Career==
Following the [[Iranian Revolution]] Haddad-Adel became a member of the [[Islamic Republic Party]] and he served in many governmental posts, including deputy culture and Islamic guidance minister (1979) and deputy education minister (1982–1993).<ref name=ireview/> Since 1995 he has been serving as the head of the Iranian [[Academy of Persian Language and Literature]] (except for August 2004 – 2008).<ref name=ireview/> He is also the executive director of the [[Encyclopaedia Islamica Foundation]]. He contributed to the establishment of the national [[International science olympiad|Scientific Olympiads]] in Iran.

Haddad-Adel served at the Majlis for thirteen years, over four terms.<ref name=ireview/> He officially ranked as the 33rd candidate of [[Tehran]] in the [[2000 Iran Majlis election|2000 parliamentary election]] after recounts by the [[Council of Guardians]] which led to an annulment of 700,000 Tehrani votes and the removal of [[Alireza Rajaei]] and Ali Akbar Rahmani from the top 30, and the withdrawal of [[Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani]]. Haddad-Adel collected the most votes from Tehran four years later, while most Tehranis refused to vote in [[2004 Iran Majlis election|2004 election]] because many [[reformist]] candidates where not allowed to run. He was supported by the [[Abadgaran]] alliance and became the Speaker of Parliament for one year beginning 6 June 2004, with 226 votes out of 259, running unopposed. He became the first non-clerical speaker since the revolution.<ref name=yonah>{{cite book|author1=Yonah Alexander|author2=Milton M. Hoenig|title=The New Iranian Leadership: Ahmadinejad, Terrorism, Nuclear Ambition, and the Middle East|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_ac30INKAu4C&pg=PA43|access-date=13 August 2013|year=2008|publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-275-99639-0|pages=42}}</ref> From 2008 to 2026, he served as an advisor to Supreme Leader [[Ali Khamenei]].<ref name=ireview/> In 2012, he ran for the Majlis speakership, but lost the bid.<ref name=katzman13>{{cite web|last=Katzman|first=Kenneth|title=Iran: U.S. Concerns and Policy Responses|url=http://www.fas.org/sgp/crs/mideast/RL32048.pdf|work=Congressional Research Service|access-date=3 August 2013|format=CRS Report for US Congress|date=17 June 2013}}</ref>

He is also a member of the [[High Council of Cultural Revolution]] and the [[Expediency Discernment Council]].

===Speaker of Parliament===
As the speaker of Parliament, Haddad-Adel condemned the bombings of the [[al-Askari Shrine]] in [[2006 al-Askari mosque bombing|2006]] and [[2007 al-Askari mosque bombing|2007]]. He added that Islamic countries must promote solidarity through guaranteeing unity and security against common enemies. In January 2008 Haddad-Adel visited [[Cairo]] for talks with then-President [[Hosni Mubarak]], making him the first senior Iranian parliamentary official to conduct high-level talks with Egyptian counterparts after the Islamic revolution.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v9sCvUDcxk4C&q=Gholam+Ali+Haddad-Adel&pg=PA25|author=Casey L. Addis|title=Iran: Regional Perspectives and U. S. Policy|year=2010|publisher=DIANE Publishing|isbn=9781437925289}}</ref>

===Presidential candidacy===
{{see also|Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel 2013 presidential campaign}}
In October 2012 Haddad-Adel formed a coalition named ''2+1'' together with [[Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf]] and [[Ali Akbar Velayati]] in October 2012, ahead of the [[2013 Iranian presidential election|upcoming presidential election]]. He withdrew his candidacy a few days before the election, and said in a statement carried by the semi-official [[Mehr News Agency]]: "With my withdrawal I ask the dear people to strictly observe the criteria of the Supreme Leader of the Revolution [Khamenei] when they vote for candidates."

He did not endorse a single candidate, but called for a hardline conservative victory. "I advise the dear people to take a correct decision so that either a conservative wins in the first round, or if the election runs to a second round, the competition between two conservatives."<ref>[https://www.haaretz.com/2013-06-10/ty-article/.premium/conservative-drops-out-of-iranian-election/0000017f-f655-d887-a7ff-fef548dd0000 Conservative drops out of Iranian presidential election] Haaretz</ref><ref>[https://edition.cnn.com/2013/06/10/world/meast/iran-elections/?hpt=hp_t3 Candidate quits Iran presidential race] ''CNN'', 10 June 2013</ref>

==President of Academy of Persian Language and Literature==
{{see also|Academy of Persian Language and Literature}}

Haddad-Adel is also the second president of the [[Academy of Persian Language and Literature]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.persianacademy.ir/fa/association.aspx|title=فرهنگستان زبان و ادب فارسی|publisher=Persian Academy|access-date=23 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414134658/http://persianacademy.ir/fa/association.aspx|archive-date=14 April 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> His presidency at the academy has focused on language policy and planning, and promotion of the Persian language in all domains.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rkgWlfVQfocC&q=academy+of+persian+language+and+literature&pg=PA110|author=Angel Lin, Peter W. Martin|title=Decolonisation, Globalisation: Language-in-education Policy and Practice|year=2005|page=110|publisher=Multilingual Matters|isbn=1853598240}}</ref>

==Affiliation==
Haddad-Adel is a senior member in the conservative umbrella organizations [[Alliance of Builders of Islamic Iran]],<ref>{{Citation|last1=Sinkaya|first1=Bayram|year =2015|title=The Revolutionary Guards in Iranian Politics: Elites and Shifting Relations|publisher=Routledge|pages=168|isbn=978-1317525646}}</ref> as well as the [[Popular Front of Islamic Revolution Forces]] (JAMNA)<ref name="ID">{{cite web|url=http://www.irdiplomacy.ir/en/page/1967380/Final+Attempts+toward+a+Principlist+Coalition+to+Block+Rouhani%E2%80%99s+Reelection.html|title=Final Attempts toward a Principlist Coalition to Block Rouhani's Reelection|date=25 February 2017|publisher=Iranian Diplomacy|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref> and is considered close to the [[Society of Devotees of the Islamic Revolution]] and the [[Society of Pathseekers of the Islamic Revolution]].<ref>{{Citation|author=Banafsheh Keynoush|title= Iran after Ahmadinejad|journal=Survival: Global Politics and Strategy|publisher=Springer Science+Business Media|place=New York|year=2012|volume=54|issue= 3|doi=10.1080/00396338.2012.690988|pages=127–146|s2cid= 153661674}}</ref>

==Public image==
According to a poll conducted in March 2016 by ''Information and Public Opinion Solutions LLC'' (iPOS) among Iranian citizens, Haddad-Adel has 51% approval and 27% disapproval ratings and thus a +24% net popularity; while 13% of responders don't know him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ipos.me/polls/2016/05/24/zarif/|title= ظریف محبوب‌ترین چهره سیاسی ایران |work=Information and Public Opinion Solutions LLC|date=24 May 2016|access-date=24 May 2016|language=fa}}</ref>

==Views==
One of Haddad-Adel's most significant views has been on the hijab in western civilization. According to him in the book of ''[[The Culture of Nakedness and the Nakedness of Culture]]'', the issue of veiling and clothing in the West is problematic. He believes that materialism is the mentality which is governed by Western culture. The culture is based on the priority of material life, with no value in anything beyond materialism. The origin of materialism as a worldview is humanism, according to the renaissance.<ref>{{cite book|author=Pamela Karimi|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uSNZXI-6M0EC&q=Gholam+Ali+Haddad-Adel&pg=PA157|title=Domesticity and Consumer Culture in Iran: Interior Revolutions of the Modern Era|year=2013|page=157|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1135101374}}</ref> According to Haddad-Adel, religion serves an important role in Iranian education. Referring to the dominance of religious thought in education, he pointed out that religious education is one result of the victory of the Islamic revolution.<ref>{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=rOJsCQAAQBAJ&q=Gholam-Ali+Haddad-Adel&pg=PA120|author= Colin Brock, Lila Zia Levers|title= Aspects of Education in the Middle East and Africa|page=101|year= 2007|publisher= Symposium Books Ltd|isbn= 978-1873927212}}</ref> He believes that the problem of human freedom is a permanent one. The problem itself has changed with the appearance of new theories in scientific and philosophic domains, particularly in the field of anthropology.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.noormags.ir/view/fa/articlepage/285903/%d9%86%d8%b8%d8%b1%db%8c-%d8%a8%d9%87-%d9%85%d9%86%d8%b8%d8%b1%d9%87-%d8%a2%d8%b2%d8%a7%d8%af%db%8c?q=%D8%BA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C%20%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%84&score=121.4963&rownumber=18|author=Gholam Ali Hadad Adel|title=A glance on the perspective of freedom|year=2006|pages=43–58}}</ref> He is also an admirer of the development of non-governmental higher education, and believes that developing such schools would lead to decreased demands on the administration of education and pedagogy.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.noormags.ir/view/fa/articlepage/968595/%da%af%d9%81%d8%aa%da%af%d9%88-%d8%a8%d8%a7-%d8%b5%d8%a7%d8%ad%d8%a8%d9%86%d8%b8%d8%b1%d8%a7%d9%86-%d9%88-%d8%a7%d8%b3%d8%a7%d8%aa%db%8c%d8%af%d8%af%d8%a7%d9%86%d8%b4%da%af%d8%a7%d9%87%d8%9b-%d8%b6%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b1%d8%aa-%d8%a8%d8%b1%d9%86%d8%a7%d9%85%d9%87-%d8%b1%db%8c%d8%b2%db%8c-%d8%a8%d8%b1%d8%a7%db%8c-%d8%aa%d9%88%d8%b3%d8%b9%d9%87-%d9%81%d8%b9%d8%a7%d9%84%db%8c%d8%aa-%d9%87%d8%a7%db%8c-%d8%a2%d9%85%d9%88%d8%b2%d8%b4%db%8c-%d8%a8%d8%b1%d8%a7%db%8c-%d8%a7%d8%b1%d8%aa%d9%82%d8%a7%db%8c-%d8%ac%d8%a7%db%8c%da%af%d8%a7|title=A conversation with professors on development of Highly education in Iran|magazine= Name Otaghe Bazargani|page=23|year=2011}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Tayebeh Mahroozadeh.jpg|thumb|Tayyebeh Mahrouzadeh, Haddad-Adel's wife, in 2016]]
Haddad-Adel is married to Tayyebeh Mahrouzadeh with whom he has one son and three daughters.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nwsiw.alzahra.ac.ir/fa/dr-mahrouzadeh-cv |title=بیوگرافی خانم دکتر طیبه ماهرو زاده|access-date=8 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615002019/http://nwsiw.alzahra.ac.ir/fa/dr-mahrouzadeh-cv |archive-date=15 June 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Their daughter Zahra married [[Mojtaba Khamenei]], the son of [[Ali Khamenei]], [[Supreme Leader of Iran]].<ref name=ewatch>{{cite web|title=Mohammad Reza Aref|url=http://iranelectionwatch.com/potential-candidates/|publisher=Iran Election Watch|access-date=13 February 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130204000341/http://iranelectionwatch.com/potential-candidates/|archive-date=4 February 2013}}</ref><ref name=bazoobandi>{{cite journal|last=Bazoobandi|first=Sara|title=The 2013 presidential election in Iran|journal=MEI Insight|date=11 January 2013|volume=88|url=http://www.mei.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/Download-Insight-88-Bazoobandi-HERE.pdf|access-date=18 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925215736/https://www.mei.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/Download-Insight-88-Bazoobandi-HERE.pdf|archive-date=25 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> This has led to the popular belief that he was among the most trusted and backed allies of Ayatollah Khamenei.<ref name=bazoobandi/> Zahra was [[Assassination of Ali Khamenei|killed along with her father-in-law]] in the U.S.–Israeli airstrikes during the [[2026 Iran war]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/dari/articles/crm8lp2ndwyo|title=درباره همسر علی خامنه‌ای و دیگر اعضای خانواده‌اش که کشته شدند، چه می‌دانیم؟|trans-title=What do we know about the wife of Ali Khamenei and the other members of his family who were killed?|work=BBC Persian|date=3 March 2026|access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref>

===Translations===
* ''Tamhidaat: Moghaddame-i baraaye har Maa-ba'd-ot-tabi'e-ye Aayande ke be onvaan-e yek Elm Arze Shavad'', a translation of [[Immanuel Kant]]'s ''[[Prolegomena to any Future Metaphysics]]'', Iran University Press, Tehran, 1988.
* ''Nazariye-ye Ma'refat dar Falsafe-ye Kaant'', a translation of Justus Hartnack's ''Kant's Theory of Knowledge'', Fekr-e Rooz, Tehran, 2000.
* ''Translation of [[Quran]]''
He translated [[Quran]] to Persian. The translation of the Quran by him lasted for 9 years. He tried to use all new and old translations and consult with other scholars of the Quran during the translation. The book has been exhibited in the nineteenth international fair of the Quran in Iran. He tried to pave the way for a more easy understanding of the Quran for all.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.noormags.ir/view/fa/articlepage/960668/%d8%a7%d8%ae%d8%a8%d8%a7%d8%b1-%d8%aa%d8%b1%d8%ac%d9%85%d9%87?q=%D8%BA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%B9%D9%84%DB%8C%20%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%AF%D9%84&score=161.20471&rownumber=5|author=Murteza Kariminia|title=Reports of translation|magazine=Tarjoman Vahy|year=2011|volume=29 |issue=15 |page=121}}</ref> The translation of Quran according to Hadad is based on the conceptual translation. He pointed out that since many Persian people could not read very well Arabic language then he undertake the task.<ref>{{cite book|author=Ali Najjarpourian, Ramazanali Gorji|url=http://www.noormags.ir/view/fa/articlepage/901073/%d8%a7%d8%b2-%d9%82%d8%b1%d8%a2%d9%86-%d8%a8%d9%87-%d9%81%d8%a7%d8%b1%d8%b3%db%8c-%d8%aa%d8%b1%d8%ac%d9%85%d9%87-%c2%ab%d9%85%d9%81%d9%87%d9%88%d9%85-%d8%a8%d9%87-%d9%85%d9%81%d9%87%d9%88%d9%85%c2%bb-%da%a9%d8%b1%d8%af%d9%85|title=I translate Quran into persian concept by concept|magazine=Roshde-e- Amoozesh Quran|year=2012|page=13}}</ref>

In 2019, he published a travelogue titled ''I Went to the Desert and Found a Downpour of Love''. Haddad-Adel describes his personal memories and experiences during the 2017 [[Arba'in pilgrimage|Arba'in trip]] in this book. Additionally, he provides a report on this spiritual journey, the emotions of those present at the annual ritual, and the mawkib keepers and organizers who host and assist those traveling to Imam Hussein's (AS) shrine in Karbala for the Arbaeen celebration.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/440885/Gholam-Ali-Haddad-Adel-publishes-travelog-of-Arbaeen-pilgrimage | title= Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel publishes travelog of Arbaeen pilgrimage | date= 7 October 2019 | publisher = Tehran Times }}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
* In 2019 the organizers of The 17th [[Golden Pen Awards]] honored Gholam-Ali Haddad-Adel as the Literary Figure of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/437742/Golden-Pen-Awards-held-without-winners-except-for-poetry-research | title= Golden Pen Awards held without winners except for poetry, research | date= 5 July 2019 | publisher = Tehran Times }}</ref>
